candidates.title: Preserve V2 outcome exit codes in the standalone implement command
candidates.problem: implement() correctly preserves typed V2 exit codes such as blocked=20, not-eligible=21, and cancelled=130, but the standalone CLI converts every non-failed result to exit 0. Shell automation can therefore interpret blocked, cancelled, or malformed missing-issue execution as success.
candidates.solution: Validate --issue at the CLI boundary and return the implement result's semantic exitCode instead of reducing outcomes to failed versus non-failed.
benefits: Makes process status agree with the printed and typed execution outcome.
Prevents schedulers from treating blocked or cancelled implementation as successful.
Makes invalid standalone invocations fail clearly.
verification: Add subprocess-level tests covering review-ready, blocked, not-eligible, cancelled, and missing --issue outcomes.
candidates.risk: Low; the change affects only standalone CLI exit semantics, although callers currently relying on incorrect zero exits will begin detecting failures.

residualRisks: The local runner files are currently untracked, so this candidate assumes they are intended repository content.
